tasks.title: Pitched roof stairs take the material of the roof they belong to
tasks.notes:
Raised 2026-10-28 from the dark-stairs-in-a-brick-roof issue (I-023, snag S-030); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. A roof column takes its material from its lidar zone alone (roof_material_for_zone, lib/builds/feature_build.py, called at about lines 1559 and 1589). zone_ridge_half_steps (about line 447) treats a whole zone as pitched when any of it rises 1 m or more, so a lower zone's material climbs the slope of a higher roof: in one rebuilt roof 363 stairs of the lower zone's material appeared and 117 of them touched main-roof columns. Not verified when written: how the eave rows land in the lower zone (the exact-tie idea in snap_to_levels is unproven and ties are rare; the nearest-level snap plus mode_filter and bucket_zones is a likelier source; no zone-grid dump yet); the roof in game. Deliver: a sloped column takes the material of the roof it rises from, not only its zone's material; the spec stays the owner of zone_materials; no old path is removed, only the zone-only lookup. The tie-break change is out of scope; file it separately only if a zone-grid dump shows ties happen. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py (roof_material_for_zone and its callers, zone_ridge_half_steps), lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (already has the snap test), and the zone_materials text in rules/feature-builds.md. Related: #126 (zone materials), #125 (pitched zones). Blocked by the roof stair task (#169) because both touch the pitched-zone code path. Proof: unit tests with two zone levels asserting each column's material. Check: re-run the dry run for the zoned feature in the snag and count stairs of the lower zone's material that touch only main-roof columns (expect 0), and look at the roof in game. Helps: any zoned pitched feature that gives each zone its own material.

Owner-authorized scope update 2026-10-28: height geometry cannot distinguish a real narrow dark lower roof from a mis-zoned brick eave. Extend the spec with explicit roof membership: roofs[label].material_regions=[{level:49,polygon:[[x,z],...]}]. Resolve region levels through existing zone_materials/default; unassigned columns retain zone lookup. Remove speculative propagation. Validate and test, independently review and ship; real-feature validation uses a temporary spec only. DRY RUNS ONLY; no world/spec writes or live Minecraft changes.

tasks.title: Decor places permanent lidar-detected objects, using photo plus lidar to skip vehicles
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 after the I-026 rebuild (#172 landed). Cause class: Capability. Ground now builds bare terrain only, so objects the lidar sees above it (surface minus terrain: planters, kiosks, bins, bollards, cars) are built by nothing: decor_plan and street_furniture use only map, aerial and designer plans and never read lidar. Deliver: decor takes lidar object columns outside footprints and trees, groups them into objects, and places one only when a street photo or the aerial identifies it as permanent furniture; vehicles and other transient objects are dropped by design (a parked car must not be built). Owner's rule: needs photo plus lidar together to place objects and avoid cars. Check decor_plan/street_furniture for an existing photo or aerial classification step to reuse before adding one. Proof: a unit test where a lidar object column with a permanent-furniture label is placed and one labelled vehicle is not. Related: #172, I-026. Helps: every ground pass on a lidar baseline.

tasks.title: Door build places the entrance cover (awning_like) from the facade plan
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the SUSU entrance covered-area issue (I-021, snag S-027; also the covered-entrance part of I-018). Cause class: Capability. facade_plan entrances accept and validate awning_like (lib/builds/facade_plan.py) but plan_doors in lib/builds/feature_build.py never reads it; awning_like is only built from free-standing details rows. Not verified: what the SUSU portal photos show at each entrance. Deliver: after the shell and roof are built (as details() does, so the roof pass does not overwrite it), a cover is placed over each placed entrance whose awning_like.kind is not none. Two geometries: awning and covered_area = a row of roof-material bottom slabs at door top + 1, as wide as the door leaves plus 1 block each side, extending out `depth` blocks over the step-out (depth default 1 when absent or 0; covered_area simply uses the larger depth, no wall carving); porch_roof = the same slab roof plus a post at each outer front corner standing on the step-out ground. Cells inside the building mass are skipped; the door stays walkable. Unresolved entrances and kind none build nothing. Dry-run prints `door <id> cover <kind> depth <n>`. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, colocated tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (one per kind, none builds nothing, depth changes extent, unresolved entrance builds no cover, existing details awning_like row unchanged), rules/feature-builds.md (geometry per kind, plan_doors reads it). The spec edit that adds awning_like to the SUSU entrance (susu_w33830305) is part of the check, not the code change: the designer or rebuild adds it after reading the photo. Check S-027: after rebuilding susu_w33830305 with an awning_like entry on its entrance, a roof stands over the door in game and the door is still walkable.
